quotes.text: It isn’t *necessarily* a won dispute, because the dispute might still resolve as a loss if you haven’t submitted evidence.
Cardholders can only fully withdraw financial disputes—that is, a chargeback, where your account balance has been debited.
it’s difficult to set a realistic expectation for when you’ll see it reflected in your Stripe account. The cardholder’s issuer might take weeks or months to process this type of adjustment.
You can submit evidence for a dispute just one time, so you want to wait long enough for your conversation with the customer to play out, but not so long that you miss the deadline.
However, some card issuers within the network might not support late withdrawal in every case.

findings: The new and matched old captures have the same withdrawal lifecycle: cardholder asks the issuer to cancel a financial chargeback, but withdrawal does not itself mean a win, speed resolution, change Dashboard/API display, or remove the network dispute-rate count (new raw:13-23; old raw:12-22). EFWs and inquiries cannot be fully withdrawn.

Both captures require timely, one-shot evidence submission for a merchant seeking a favorable outcome even after a customer says they withdrew, and both say a refund on a disputed charge stays blocked until the issuer decides for the merchant (new raw:35-47; old raw:34-46). Customer withdrawal confirmation is helpful, explicitly not required.

Both captures preserve fee and decision boundaries: a countered fee may apply in addition to the received fee; it is returned on a win, while the received fee generally is not; Mexico and Japan are excepted from the countered fee (new raw:49-53; old raw:48-52). The cardholder's bank, not Stripe or customer agreement, decides the dispute, potentially over up to three months.

Both captures say card networks permit late withdrawal even after a loss, but some issuers may not support it in every case (new raw:61; old raw:60). Late adjustments often occur outside the regular network lifecycle: the issuer might take weeks or months to process one, while a realistic date for its reflection in Stripe is difficult to set (new raw:63; old raw:62). Correct current source:38,40 and disputes concept:133; the existing summaries overstate issuer acceptance and the timing certainty. This is a pre-existing retained-claim correction, not a new November rule.

The fee wording is from a dated capture and points to a linked pricing page that was not reviewed in this job; no current account-specific fee amount or contractual exception is inferred.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/withdrawing, the new capture confirms the same central lifecycle as the matched old one: a cardholder asks their issuer to withdraw a financial chargeback, but it is not automatically won and still counts against dispute rate (new raw:15-23; old raw:14-22). To seek a win, the merchant must submit evidence by the deadline even after the customer's assurance; a disputed-charge refund remains blocked until the issuer decides favorably (new raw:35-47; old raw:34-46). The mapped [[source-stripe-disputes-withdrawals]] summary preserves these core boundaries. An EFW or inquiry cannot be fully withdrawn, and customer confirmation is optional evidence, not the final issuer decision.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/withdrawing, the old and new captures have no substantive behavioral change; the diff adds formatting and see-also navigation. Nevertheless, [[source-stripe-disputes-withdrawals]] needs a bounded current-claim correction at lines 38 and 40, with a reciprocal disputes concept correction at line 133. All networks allow a late withdrawal request, but a particular issuer might not support it and must decide whether it is allowed (old raw:60; new raw:61). The issuer might take weeks or months to process an adjustment, while its reflection date in Stripe is difficult to predict (old raw:62; new raw:63); neither is a guaranteed timeline after contact. Preserve the dated withdrawn-versus-won, one-shot evidence, refund, and fee conditions (old raw:40-52; new raw:41-53).
